text.en: Asha wanted to paint a box-shaped cupboard. "How much paint?" she asked. "Find the surface area," said her teacher.

Heron's formula gives the area of a triangle from its three sides a, b and c: area = sqrt(s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)) where s is half the perimeter. It is used to find the area of a triangle when no height is known, and to find the area of a quadrilateral by splitting it into two triangles.
A cuboid has length l, breadth b and height h. Its total surface area is 2(lb + bh + hl), its lateral surface area is 2h(l + b) and its volume is l x b x h. A cube of side a has surface area 6a^2 and volume a^3.
Area is measured in square units and volume in cubic units.

It is used to find the area of a triangle when no height is known, and to find the area of a quadrilateral by splitting it into two triangles.
A cuboid has length l, breadth b and height h.
Its total surface area is 2(lb + bh + hl), its lateral surface area is 2h(l + b) and its volume is l x b x h.
A cube of side a has surface area 6a^2 and volume a^3.
Area is measured in square units and volume in cubic units.
Choose what to measure before choosing a formula. A ribbon around a shape measures perimeter, paper covering its face measures area, and space inside a solid measures volume.
A triangle with sides six, seven and nine has perimeter twenty-two. The semiperimeter is half of that, so s is eleven.
Check that the two shorter sides add to more than the longest side before applying Heron’s formula. For six, seven and nine, thirteen is greater than nine.
In Heron’s expression, subtract each side from eleven. The resulting factors are five, four and two, and we multiply them by eleven.
Take the square root last. The exact area is two times the square root of one hundred ten. A decimal approximation is about twenty point nine eight square units.
Try sides four, four and eight. The two shortest lengths add to exactly eight. The sides can lie in a straight line but do not enclose a triangle of positive area.
For three, four and five, the semiperimeter is six. Heron’s formula gives the square root of six times three times two times one, which is six square units.
If a triangle is already right-angled and its perpendicular sides are three and four, half their product gives the same area. This is a useful independent check.
To find a quadrilateral’s area, choose a diagonal that lies inside the shape and separates it into distinct triangles. Count the diagonal as a side in each calculation.
Two triangles can share the same diagonal and still have different perimeters. Calculate one semiperimeter for each triangle using its own three side lengths.

board.text: Use a separate s for each triangle

text.en: After finding both triangle areas, add them for the whole quadrilateral. The diagonal itself contributes length to the calculations without adding a strip of area.
For a cuboid, unfold the six faces in your mind. The top and bottom have dimensions length by breadth. The four other faces have height as one of their dimensions.
Two of the upright faces are length by height. The other two are breadth by height. Counting all six faces gives the total surface area.
The lateral surface of a box with a designated base is the set of side faces. Leave the top and bottom out of this measurement.
For eight by five by three centimetres, the side faces total two times three times thirteen, which is seventy-eight square centimetres.
The top and bottom each cover forty square centimetres. Add both faces to seventy-eight to get one hundred fifty-eight square centimetres for the closed box.
If that same box has no lid, subtract only the top face of forty square centimetres from the closed total. The bottom is still present.
Volume counts how many unit cubes could fit inside. A base eight by five holds forty cubes in each layer. Three layers make one hundred twenty cubic centimetres.
A cube has three equal dimensions. With side four centimetres, each face covers sixteen square centimetres and there are six faces.
The same cube has four layers of sixteen unit cubes. It has volume sixty-four cubic centimetres, using cubic units rather than square units.
Double every edge of a cube. Each square face becomes four times as large, and cubic volume becomes eight times as large. Follow the two or three length factors to see why.

board.text: Scale factor 2 → area factor 4, volume factor 8

text.en: When a rectangular box’s volume and base dimensions are known, divide volume by base area to find its height. A volume of one hundred twenty over base area forty gives height three centimetres.

If measurements use mixed units, convert before substituting. A length of one metre and a breadth of fifty centimetres become one hundred centimetres and fifty centimetres when computing square centimetres.

board.text: Choose one length unit before multiplying

text.en: Check your answer by naming the actual surface or space measured. A box label needs area, a ribbon around its base needs length, and storage capacity needs volume.

problem.en: A rectangular box is 8 cm long, 5 cm broad and 3 cm high. Find its lateral area, closed total surface area and volume.

text.en: Find the four side areas. Multiply twice the height by the sum of length and breadth.

why.en: Two times three times thirteen gives seventy-eight square centimetres.

text.en: Add two faces of eight by five to the lateral area.

why.en: The closed box has one hundred fifty-eight square centimetres of surface area.

text.en: Multiply eight by five by three to find the space within the box.

why.en: The volume is one hundred twenty cubic centimetres.

requiredIdeas.en: Volume is the product l x b x h.
